title: What on a tree or in a village has a count of four or five digits?
description: Farhan sits by a banyan tree in his village. The video estimates leaves, people and vehicles from a part and the number of parts, and says other reasoned answers are fine.
teaching_notes: One idea: a part multiplied by the number of parts gives a 4 or 5 digit count. Watch for children who stop at the count of one branch.

source: Finding large numbers, a tree and a village
video_script.why: The child must name 4 digit and 5 digit counts about a tree and their own place, and different children will name different ones.
video_script.substitution: Count a small part, such as leaves on one branch, then multiply by the number of parts.
video_script.anchor: Farhan sitting by a huge banyan tree beside the village pond in Bihar
video_script.wrong_answer: the tree has one hundred and fifty leaves
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu says the tree has one hundred and fifty leaves because one branch does. That counts only one branch; a tree has many branches.
video_script.payoff_line: a part multiplied by the number of parts

final_answer.value: Sample answer: leaves on a tree, 6,000; people in a village, 2,500; vehicles in a town, 15,000 (answers will differ)
final_answer.spoken: for example six thousand leaves on a tree, two thousand five hundred people in a village and fifteen thousand vehicles in a town, and other reasoned answers are fine

hold_back: Sample answer: leaves on a tree, 6,000; people in a village, 2,500; vehicles in a town, 15,000 (answers will differ)
never_show: a single right answer for every child
maths_rules: tree: 40 branches, about 150 leaves each: 40 × 150 = 6,000 leaves; 4 digits
big banyan: about 100 branches, about 150 leaves each: 100 × 150 = 15,000 leaves, more than 10,000; 5 digits
village: about 500 houses, about 5 people in each: 500 × 5 = 2,500 people; 4 digits
town: about 300 streets, about 50 vehicles on each: 300 × 50 = 15,000 vehicles; 5 digits
other answers are fine when the child can name the part and the number of parts
slip: 150 leaves is the count of one branch only
video_script.design: One idea: a part multiplied by the number of parts. Wrong idea: use the count of one part as the count of the whole. The banyan and the village stay in the anchor band; the samples build on the stage. Open prompt: other reasoned answers are fine.

beats.on_screen: a photo of the big tree sits behind as a dimmed backdrop and fades at the end of the beat; a small title card From your book; a huge banyan tree beside a village pond; two empty lists: on the tree, in the village or town; each wants counts with 4 or 5 digits

marks.m119: the small title card From your book appears
marks.m120: a huge banyan tree beside a village pond appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m119'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m120'/>Farhan's village in Bihar has a huge banyan tree beside the pond.
<bookmark mark='m121'/>Name some things on the tree whose count has four or five digits.
<bookmark mark='m122'/>Then name some things in your village, town or city.

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.m123: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='m123'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a hint card in the working band: think of things that come in many groups; leaves on a branch; people in a house

marks.m124: the words many equal groups light up
marks.m125: the words leaves on a branch light up
marks.m126: the words people in a house light up

narration: <bookmark mark='m124'/>Think of things that come in many equal groups.
<bookmark mark='m125'/>For a tree, think of the leaves on one branch and the number of branches.
<bookmark mark='m126'/>For a village, think of people in a house and the number of houses.
<bookmark mark='m127'/>Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows one branch, 150 leaves, so the tree has 150 leaves; one branch is circled on the tree; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.m128: Chintu's bubble appears with one branch, 150 leaves
marks.m129: one branch of the tree is circled
marks.m130: the other branches of the tree glow, and the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m128'/>One branch has one hundred and fifty leaves, so the tree has one hundred and fifty leaves.
<bookmark mark='m129'/>That counts only one branch.
<bookmark mark='m130'/>A tree has many branches, so we must use all of them.

beats.on_screen: a tree with 40 branches of about 150 leaves: 40 × 150 = 6,000; a huge banyan with 100 branches: 100 × 150 = 15,000, more than 10,000

marks.m131: the tree with 40 branches appears, each marked about 150 leaves

narration: <bookmark mark='m131'/>Take a tree with forty branches, and about one hundred and fifty leaves on each.
<bookmark mark='m132'/>That is about six thousand leaves, which is a four digit count.
<bookmark mark='m133'/>A huge banyan has about one hundred branches with one hundred and fifty leaves each.
<bookmark mark='m134'/>That makes fifteen thousand leaves, more than ten thousand, so it is a five digit count.

beats.on_screen: a village with 500 houses and about 5 people in each: 500 × 5 = 2,500; a town with 300 streets and about 50 vehicles on each: 300 × 50 = 15,000; the words other answers are fine glow

marks.m135: a village with 500 houses and about 5 people in each appears
marks.m137: a town with 300 streets and about 50 vehicles on each appears
marks.m140: the words other answers are fine glow

narration: <bookmark mark='m135'/>A village has about five hundred houses, with about five people in each house.
<bookmark mark='m136'/>Five hundred houses of five people make two thousand five hundred people.
<bookmark mark='m137'/>A town has about three hundred streets, with about fifty vehicles on each.
<bookmark mark='m138'/>Three hundred streets of fifty vehicles make fifteen thousand vehicles.
<bookmark mark='m139'/>Each answer is a part multiplied by the number of parts.
<bookmark mark='m140'/>Your own village will give different numbers, and that is fine.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the tree and the village; two check lines appear: count the digits of your answer; say the part and the number of parts

marks.m141: the check line count the digits appears
marks.m142: the check line the part and the number of parts appears
marks.m143: the line many answers are right appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m141'/>Check each answer by counting its digits.
<bookmark mark='m142'/>Then say the part and the number of parts.
<bookmark mark='m143'/>Many answers are right when you can give a reason.
